comment: How far apart two scientific interpretations are, and how bad the difference is. One versioned file instead of two arrays of field names in Rust: changing what this project considers a serious error is now a visible edit to data, not a constant somebody moved.

axioms.note: These three numbers are constrained so that the resulting tree edit distance is a genuine metric. distance.rs refuses to load a file that breaks them, and property tests check the axioms on random AST pairs.
axioms.kind_change_at_most_twice_delete: kind_change <= delete + insert, or the triangle inequality fails when a relabel is compared against delete-then-insert
axioms.relabel_capped_at_kind_change: a relabel never costs more than changing what the node is; the sum of field weights is capped at kind_change
axioms.symmetry: there is no asymmetric weight anywhere. An asymmetric cost would make d(a,b) != d(b,a), balls would stop being balls, and any later clustering or caching of distances would be quietly wrong

symbol.why: O vs S is a different element

arrow.why: → vs ⇌ is a different claim about the reaction

direction.why: which side the limit is approached from

alphabet.why: Latin p and Greek ρ are different quantities

kind.why: fallback for any variant tag not named below; kept at the class it had before this file existed

Derivative.kind.why: an ordinary derivative is not a partial one

coefficient.why: 2H₂ vs H₂ — how much of it reacts

order.why: a second derivative is not a first

case.why: ΔG and Δg are different quantities

marker.why: the state annotation (aq), (s) — a real claim, a small edit

condition.why: «при нагревании» over the arrow: a serious claim carried by a short string. Its class and its weight disagree on purpose — see the note below

Group.kind.why: round versus square brackets around the same expression: presentation, not meaning. This is the «изменение пробела» end of the scale

note_on_class_versus_weight: severity and weight answer different questions and are deliberately not forced to agree. severity says WHAT changed — a categorical fact, and the thing a release gate counts. weight says HOW FAR the answer moved. `condition` is the clearest case: changing the reaction condition is a serious claim (S3) carried by one short string (0.2). Collapsing the two into one number would lose whichever question was not asked.
